interfaces.name: IPipelineServiceTask
interfaces.summary: A service task defined as a pipeline: ordered durable stages followed by the one conclusion, composed in Define. The conclusion is a final step for work that finishes by itself or by polling, or a reply terminal for work answered by a message into a mailbox a stage opened. A task that does one thing should implement IServiceTask instead — this interface specialized to just the concluding step.

interfaces.name: IProcessStepConfigurable
interfaces.summary: Implemented by process handlers (service tasks and task/process lifecycle hooks) that want to override the workflow engine's default execution timeout and/or retry strategy for the step that runs them. This is the most specific tier in the resolution order: implementation override → command default → engine default.

interfaces.name: IServiceTask
interfaces.summary: A service task that does one thing: a single unit of work executed (and on failure, retried) durably by the workflow engine when the process enters a BPMN service task. This is the shape almost every service task wants. A task with several consecutive units of work — dispatch then await, or a series of API calls — should implement IPipelineServiceTask instead and give each unit its own durable stage.
